A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Bonsai node-classification work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite terminology changes and relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original accuracy, runtime, cross-architecture, ablation, and parameter-sensitivity results in Section 4 and Appendix B.

after.justification: v3 retains original experiments and adds benchmark comparisons, gradient-correlation results, expanded ablations, and carbon-emissions estimates.

M1.justification: WL embeddings, sampled reverse-k-NN, greedy exemplar selection, and iterative PPR sparsification/enrichment remain unchanged. The PPR procedure moves from Section 3.3 to Appendix A.4; expanded explanations and explicit reverse-k-NN input in Algorithm 1 do not establish a different algorithm.

E1.justification: v3 adds MAG240M to the six retained benchmarks. The evaluated graph has 1,398,159 nodes and 153 classes (Table 3), substantially extending node and label-space scale beyond v1, while retaining the node-classification task.

E2.justification: EXGC, GC-SNTK, and GEOM join the evaluated accuracy and condensation-time comparisons, substantially expanding the competitor set. Random node selection also becomes an explicit comparator in the component ablation. Table 5 retains its original comparator set.

E3.justification: Cross-architecture accuracy evaluation expands from 1% compression to 0.5%, 1%, and 3%, and the ablation explicitly tests all three budgets. MAG240M introduces an 80:10:10 split; the original datasets retain 60:20:20. New gradient-correlation and estimated-carbon evaluations broaden the evaluation design; runtime revisions alone do not establish changed training procedures.

E4.justification: The component ablation expands from three datasets in v1 Figure 4b to six datasets across three budgets in v3 Figure 4, adding Random to distinguish random nodes from random computation trees. New Table 2 tests the connection between WL-embedding similarities and training gradients. Existing sampling-size and k sensitivity analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both versions already specify five repetitions and report means and standard deviations. v3 additionally reports correlation p-values and explicitly invokes p < 0.05 significance in Table 2; this does not establish an increase in repeated runs.

E6.justification: New competitors overturn Bonsai's Ogbn-arxiv lead at 0.5% and 1%, despite unchanged Bonsai accuracies. Reddit Herding timeouts become accuracies of 81.72, 83.48, and 88.51. Reported Reddit greedy time changes from 275.52 to 0.696 seconds (v1 Table 6; v3 Table 7), without an explained procedural change. Numerous benchmark, correlation, and emissions results are added; the earlier edge-count table and Flickr/Ogbn-arxiv 0.5% training-time panels are removed.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, sampling bound, NP-hardness argument, monotonicity/submodularity proofs, approximation guarantee, and complexity derivation are retained. PPR equations relocate to Appendix A.4 and other equations are renumbered without substantive mathematical revision.

C1.justification: The central gradient-free, linear-time, model-agnostic contribution remains. Evaluation claims expand from six to seven datasets; the main-text speed comparison changes from 22-times versus GDEM to over seven-times versus newly added EXGC, and environmental benefits become a quantified 17-times claim. The abstract still retains the 22-times statement.

C2.justification: v1 generally attributes greater importance to reverse-k-NN, except on Reddit. v3 develops a budget-dependent explanation: higher-degree exemplars make PPR increasingly important at larger budgets. It also explains the information tradeoff between random nodes and random trees and elaborates how marginal coverage discourages redundant exemplar selection.

D1.justification: The reported code location changes from anonymous hosting to a named GitHub repository. Carbon-estimation hardware assumptions and conversion rates are newly documented. Core hardware, software versions, two-layer evaluation models, and k = 5 remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Table 1 substantially expands coverage of contemporary condensation methods through EXGC, GC-SNTK, and GEOM. Section 1.1 replaces the blanket fully-connected-graph critique with a node-compression versus edge-complexity argument and acknowledges sparsification. Application and carbon-accounting references are added, while the Shervashidze and Topping references are removed.

P1.justification: v3 extensively expands the representativeness, diversity, and ablation explanations while rewriting parts of the introduction and efficiency discussion. It changes distillation terminology to condensation throughout, moves detailed sparsification into the appendix, and reorganizes the experimental and reproducibility narrative.

P2.justification: Figure 3 is redrawn as a concrete toy example; accuracy tables and the ablation figure expand substantially. The condensation-time chart becomes Table 6, and correlation and emissions tables are added. The earlier edge-count table and main-text training-time figure disappear, while most existing appendix plots are retained and renumbered.

improvement.justification: The added competitive baselines and broader ablations make the unchanged method's performance boundaries and component roles easier to assess than in v1. However, unexplained runtime revisions and inconsistencies in the new emissions reporting—including Table 8's units and entries that do not follow Table 6's runtimes and the stated conversion rates—limit confidence in the strengthened efficiency claims. These tradeoffs leave a limited net quality improvement.
